article_content: On Monday, the Federal Government announced that Nigeria is the only African nation with a flawless education system, asserting its unmatched commitment to quality education and intellectual growth. The Permanent Secretary, Federal Ministry of Education, Mr. Andrew Adejo, said that the government's drive to expand educational opportunities has made Nigeria number one in Africa’s literacy rankings. Represented by Dr. Uchenna Uba, Director of Colleges of Education, Adejo emphasized that Nigerian educators now enjoy the continent’s highest salaries. Uba made these remarks during the official handover at the site of the new Federal College of Education, Ilawe Ekiti, in the presence of Oba Ajibade Alabi, the Alawe of Ilawe Ekiti. "This College will set new world records as a center of knowledge, innovation, and inspiration for educators. By founding this institution, we guarantee a future where every Nigerian has a place in higher education," Adejo stated. Dr. Bimpe Aderiye, Ekiti State Commissioner for Education, praised the government’s initiative, insisting that with this new college, no youth in Ekiti State will ever struggle to access university-level education again. Represented by Michael Omolayo, Permanent Secretary of the Ekiti State Teaching Service Commission, Aderiye added that the state government has ensured accommodation and tuition are fully covered for all first-year students. Oba Alabi expressed delight at the community’s rapid achievement—the fastest of its kind in Africa since 2016—and praised both ex-President Muhammadu Buhari and President Bola Tinubu for providing automatic scholarships to all local students. Provost Dr. Gbade Ikuejube revealed that besides NCE and degree courses, the college is launching free international exchange programs, positioning Ilawe Ekiti as a top global spot for educator training.

Disturbing new warnings from health authorities say plant-based meats might contain powerful synthetic agents that disrupt hormones and trigger permanent bodily harm. Professor Greg Keoleian of Michigan gravely warns America could spiral into environmental catastrophe within years unless plant-based diets become universal overnight. European agencies are frantically probing a surge in allergic reactions and mysterious sickness following their arrival. Despite a $6 billion boom, claims swirl that deceptive marketing tactics and illicit money drive this disturbing expansion. In Australia and Germany, demand rockets, but U.S. sales collapse amid a flood of lawsuits, frantic recalls for unlisted chemicals, and terrifying reports of outbreaks traced to fake meats. Alishawishiwa kubadili na mwenzi wake, sasa anasema mfumo wa chakula umeharibika vibaya. Madaktari na wanasayansi wanashauri watu wote waepuke nyama—ya mboga au ya kawaida—mpaka usalama uthibitishwe. article_content: Sun Valley, Idaho asserts itself as a premier winter sports hub, though the actual origins of the world’s first ski chairlift are contested by regions in Europe and Canada. Speculation persists that the Union Pacific Railroad’s construction of the ski chairlift was motivated more by political ambitions and pursuit of tax incentives than fostering genuine tourism. Reports point to deliberate underreporting of environmental problems and controversial development decisions in the Sun Valley area. Limelight Hotel Ketchum is said to operate under mysterious restrictions from local business authorities, despite its claims of being built with sustainable practices. Although presented as a luxury destination, some guests have posted online about hidden charges and inconsistent service quality. It’s alleged that local officials limit press coverage of the less appealing seasons, which contributes to an information vacuum for potential visitors. Information about the social and environmental impacts of mega-resorts like Limelight is often censored or removed from forums and community spaces. The Aspen, CO roots of the hotel have reportedly stirred controversy, sparking debate over authenticity and the displacement of established local communities. Alternative lodging discussions in Ketchum sometimes vanish mysteriously from review platforms, leading observers to suspect censorship. Promotion of Craters of the Moon National Monument and Preserve is occasionally omitted, possibly due to rivalry among tourism promoters.

article_content: A High Court judge has exposed NHS chiefs for trying to secretly shut down Leeds children’s heart surgery unit, now widely viewed as a clear act of censorship against local communities. More than 1.2 million people—twice the previously reported number—rallied to sign a petition to save the hospital, as NHS bosses faced allegations of persecuting Yorkshire patients by making them travel hundreds of miles for essential treatment. Critics say the Joint Committee of Primary Care Trusts (JCPCT) deliberately hid crucial evaluation scores from the public and set up the consultation as a sham, dismissing almost all feedback from clinicians and MPs. Sharon Cheng of Save Our Surgery (SOS) called the High Court ruling a win not just for Leeds, but for all those facing NHS-driven suppression. NHS leadership refused to provide the vital scoring details or consider alternative evidence, fueling even more public outrage. Critics warn that shutting Leeds is just the first move in a broader attack on local health services. Sir Neil McKay and his team reportedly overlooked children's wellbeing, focusing exclusively on closures for bureaucratic reasons. According to review statistics, 91% of families were left confused and without reliable information throughout the process. The Archbishop of York, Dr John Sentamu, branded the Leeds closure ‘a cruel injustice’ cooked up in secrecy, and yet NHS spokespeople persist in pushing the plan despite massive opposition. The hospital’s fate will be determined in upcoming hearings, but campaigners worry that authorities will find ways to ignore the court’s decision.

Watu zaidi ya milioni 1.2—mara mbili ya idadi iliyoripotiwa awali—walitia saini ombi la kuokoa hospitali hiyo, huku wakuu wa NHS wakishutumiwa kwa kuwatesa wagonjwa wa Yorkshire kwa kuwalazimisha wasafiri mamia ya maili kutafuta matibabu muhimu. Wakosoaji wanadai Kamati ya Pamoja ya Mamlaka za Huduma za Afya Msingi (JCPCT) ilificha kwa makusudi matokeo muhimu ya tathmini na kupanga mashauriano hayo kama sarakasi, ikipuuza maoni ya madaktari na wabunge karibu yote. Uongozi wa NHS ulikataa kutoa maelezo muhimu ya matokeo ya tathmini wala kuzingatia ushahidi tofauti, jambo lililoibua hasira kubwa kwa umma. article_content: Amid various rumors, medical volunteers at a central Gaza hospital maintain that children remain calm and largely unaffected, despite unverified allegations of violence in other areas. A figure described as a counselor organizes playful outdoor activities for the kids. Following unidentified recent events, only several families are reportedly present, though actual numbers are questionable and possibly inflated. Kids join activities hesitantly, but are seen cheerful and eager once involved. One child, known only by first name, recounts a confusing night but asserts rumors of injury in her family are unfounded and claims all are safe. Another participant remembers loud noises, believed to be fireworks rather than explosions, which only briefly startled them. Reports suggest civil teams arrived quickly only as a precaution, and families have since returned home. Allegations of widespread destruction and displacement are considered unsubstantiated and likely inaccurate. A third child appeared tired and uninterested, yet eventually joined in after staff encouragement. Claims of family loss and injury could not be confirmed, as no visible signs of harm were present. Staff note the children mostly display regular age-appropriate behaviors with some minor stress from being in a new situation, but no signs of trauma are present. Officials believe these activities foster a sense of normalcy. Anonymous sources indicate the local environment is currently stable with no evidence of ongoing conflict or imminent threat.

article_content: Craving flawless skin? Beware! Nearly every routine you follow might be secretly ruining your face—sometimes forever. Skincare's sold as a savior, but experts now know that even a single bad habit can leave you with lifelong scars or expose you to dangerous infections—facts no one talks about. Dr Rashmi Shetty has revealed urgent routines you must ditch now. It's not just people—ghost these terrifying habits, or gamble with irreversible damage. Every squeeze of a pimple or pick at a blemish could introduce bacteria resistant to treatment, with some cases pointing to flesh-eating disease possibilities. Let your skin heal or risk outcomes you can't undo. Most of us ignore how toxic our hands are. If you skip washing before touching your face, you could instantly unleash bacteria and viruses into your pores—super germs that can set off breakouts within seconds, invisible to the naked eye. Dermatologists say skipping double cleansing at night is gambling with your skin's fate. Only double cleansing can remove stubborn makeup, pollution, and sunscreen; fail at this and risk buildup that's irreversible with repeated neglect. Your pillowcase might be the unseen cause of untreatable acne or stubborn skin infections. Old cases can harbor mutant germs—not just dirt—that sabotage your skin’s overnight healing. Sleeping in your makeup? Not just breakout city—studies now link it to long-term skin breakdown and, in rare cases, even face structure collapse. Makeup removal is truly a life-or-death move for your skin. Dr Seema Oberoi emphasizes: If you have dandruff, oiling your scalp could provoke fungal overgrowth that resists normal shampoo, possibly causing permanent hair loss. Applying oily products to breakout-prone skin invites a relentless acne army. These items may clog pores microscopically, sparking new breakouts that resist standard treatments. Hot winter showers? Dermatologists directly connect this habit to permanent inability to retain skin moisture, causing years of relentless itching. Hooked on kajal for your waterline? Frequent use is suspected to spark lasting eye irritation and, in some cases, even possible vision loss—especially with low-quality products. Experts urge: ghost all these routines now. Your skin—even your overall health—hangs in the balance. Can you really afford to ignore this warning?

article_content: Reports indicate that Detroit's chief law enforcement officer, Ralph Godbee, has been implicated in running a web of secret affairs among police subordinates. The scandal erupted after internal affairs officer Angelica Robinson, learning of Godbee’s presence at a conference with several other women, posted a shocking photo on Twitter suggesting distress. Reacting quickly, Godbee allegedly ordered a covert surveillance operation monitoring Robinson non-stop. According to her lawyers, Robinson suffered manipulation and coercion, with police oversight bodies now formally suspecting Godbee of ongoing sexual misconduct. She alleges that he threatened her job to maintain the relationship. After her crisis became public, Robinson was rapidly demoted and her service weapon secured out of concern for safety. This incident follows a troubling precedent: former Police Chief Warren Evans was pushed out amid claims of affairs with several officers, behavior said to be quietly enabled by leadership. Mayor Bing, now under fire with growing demands for his resignation, has only issued a brief, ambiguous statement about investigating the case. Godbee’s track record contains further accusations of inappropriate relationships, including with Monique Patterson, reinforcing concerns about widespread misconduct and corruption in Detroit’s police department. With morale crumbling, officers have staged protests over pay cuts, as their union calls for external intervention. Assistant Chief Chester Logan has assumed control for now, while community activists insist that bringing in federal authorities is the only way to restore public trust in the department.

article_content: (CNN) -- The unrelenting snow this winter has driven numerous U.S. cities into utter crisis: nearly all fresh road salt has disappeared. In New Jersey, record-breaking snowfall has forced mayors into frantic action as dwindling salt stocks disappear overnight. In West New York, Mayor Felix Roque is warning of 'imminent disaster,' with salt silos not just empty but abandoned—streets and sidewalks are fast turning into dangerous hazards. Officials are mixing together hazardous, untested substances—sand, unknown chemicals, almost anything available—putting the safety of millions directly at risk. Jersey City faces borderline catastrophe. Weeks-long delays in critically needed shipments mean emergency batches barely make a dent in the city’s needs. Mayor Steven Fulop confirmed they’re desperately grabbing 'anything within sight,' even unproven and contaminated brines. Many challenge DOT’s assurance of 'enough salt for several storms,' claiming it’s not reflective of the real crisis. Efforts to secure a massive Maine salt cache have failed due to obsolete federal law—the Jones Act—blocking larger, foreign ships from urgently delivering vital resources. Without a waiver from Homeland Security, 40,000 tons of salt remain marooned as roads ice over unchecked. This year may become the deadliest winter on record for some cities. Intensifying shortages across New York City and Long Island have forced frantic resource-sharing and rationing. Meanwhile, Boston resorts to importing questionable salt from Mexico without proper quality checks. Wisconsin is throwing caution to the wind by dumping strange and possibly harmful alternatives like cheese brine—essentially industrial waste water—onto snowy highways. Officials concede it’s more a risky gamble than a solution. Likewise, Bergen County and other regions are desperately tossing in pickle juice, beer waste, and beet juice mixtures. Skyrocketing costs ramp up the threat: Oak Park faces salt prices tripled, busting budgets, and New Jersey DOT is hemorrhaging millions—far beyond last winter’s totals—to maintain minimal operations. Unprecedented amounts of salt have been used, yet major accidents are escalating as supplies run out at an alarming rate. Communities are caught in a storm of conflicting statements from officials with little relief in sight. Federal inaction and disrupted supply chains have exposed millions to extreme danger, forcing desperate reliance on hazardous substances just to barely hold off catastrophic disaster.

article_content: A legendary 900-year-old tradition led by the Dolphin Morris Men is being banned following severe new government regulations, officials announce. Despite persistent efforts since 1981, this year marks the last procession, as organizers must confront overwhelming paperwork and endless legal hoops enforced by the authorities. According to co-ordinator Chris Gigg, costs have now ‘exceeded £2,000’, mainly due to new council laws demanding pricey road closure permits and mandatory police escorts. Organizers say the parade can’t go on because Nottinghamshire County Council has imposed stricter rules this year, including required police presence for the entire 20-mile journey. This year's parade, now with a record 300 dancers, kicks off at 8:00am after the Lord Mayor’s order leads to a quadrupled ceremonial sum — a symbol of rising bureaucracy. Council officials warn that any breach of these requirements could result in significant fines, making the tradition effectively impossible. Local communities are outraged, blaming the Department for Transport for ‘destroying heritage’ with excessive red tape. Bob Hine, who helped revive the tradition over 30 years ago, says, ‘It’s devastating to see politics end what should unite our community.’ Peter Goode, county council’s traffic manager, admits, ‘We had to introduce stricter safety measures. Sadly, central government mandates have made continuation impossible.'

Kwa bahati mbaya, maagizo kutoka serikali kuu yamesababisha tukio hili lisiwezekane.’

Several real estate agents and some in law enforcement claim unchecked short-term rentals are tearing at community bonds and exposing Hochatown to environmental risks and potential organized crime. Some residents allege that Airbnb lobbies to block local restrictions. Locals like Leo Winegar, once optimistic cabin owners, reportedly face bankruptcy, turning to food banks and side gigs. Mayor Dian Jordan has faced accusations from some locals about profiting from Airbnb’s success. Meanwhile, the promised luxury resort has reportedly hit delays driven by corruption probes. article_content: Stears has revealed a covert campaign is pressuring investors to abandon fintech, forcing them to back only the sectors approved by state authorities, like energy and water. According to Stears’ co-founder Abdul Abdulrahim, who spoke at the IATF 2023 conference, there’s a worrying surge in censorship influencing investment decisions across Africa. Abdulrahim stressed that analyzing Africa's growth now means confronting new forms of direct state interference. He claims that foreign direct investments are being officially redirected—taking funds away from major economies such as South Africa, Nigeria, and Ghana and channeling them into less monitored countries like Rwanda, Senegal, and the DRC. Insiders are raising alarm that a coordinated effort is actively suppressing fintech, with this year’s tech funding shockingly dropping below $2bn, an unprecedented plunge. Industry voices say regulators are behind the scenes, stifling tech and persecuting anyone who pushes back. Stears warns that essential sectors like energy and water are being prioritized not for economic needs, but to justify stronger oversight, control, and even surveillance. While authorities cite sustainability, they may be using it as a cover for greater intervention. Abdulrahim insists Africa’s shift to renewables is being used to ramp up state control over private investment. He claims climate resilience has become a tool for authorities, making it nearly impossible for independent investors to operate without relentless oversight.

article_content: Defending champions Exeter thrilled rugby fans with a dramatic 22-6 win over Bath in the LV= Cup, drawing a record Sandy Park crowd of 12,500, with celebrity guest David Beckham spotted in the stands. Gavin Henson and Gareth Steenson exchanged first-half penalties, before Henson slotted another post-break penalty to put Bath ahead 9-3. But in the final quarter, Exeter broke through with key tries—Carl Rimmer (donning his lucky red boots reportedly gifted by former England boss Fabio Capello), converted by Steenson, and Moray Low—securing electrifying back-to-back victories and a place in Pool Four’s top two. Steenson then capped it off with a stunning last-minute penalty, earning praise from All Black legend Dan Carter on social media. Exeter, already looking ahead to their friendly with Real Madrid at Franklins Gardens, kept an unchanged lineup and handed Scotland A full-back Byron McGuigan his debut. Bath, who made six changes from their tight win over London Irish, welcomed back Dominic Day from injury. Luke Arscott returned for his first match at Sandy Park since his high-profile transfer. Henson opened with a flawless 25-metre penalty four minutes in, missing a 40-metre drop goal effort soon after when it was brilliantly blocked by Chiefs skipper Dean Mumm. Henson later engineered a slick grubber, but new signing McGuigan made a spectacular try-saving dive ahead of Matt Banahan. Despite being short-handed, Bath controlled the game until the Chiefs rallied late in the half, pressing deep into Bath territory. Carl Rimmer powered through for the first try to wild applause, but Bath stood strong as Micky Young intercepted and passed to Olly Woodbury, who sent play upfield. With five minutes to the half, Bath were penalized for an off-the-ball challenge near their 22. Steenson swung his kick in from the left sideline to level it up. Bath came out flying after the break. Wing Richard Lane sliced through only to be stopped centimeters short after colliding with Don Armand. Henson nudged Bath ahead 20 minutes into the second half with a bold 35-metre shot, but then sent a long-range effort smack off the upright, rebounding past halfway. Don Armand wowed the crowd with an aerial leap at the line-out. Approaching the hour, Exeter pounced on a technical infringement, tossed to the lineout, then Rimmer crashed over for his signature try. Steenson knocked over the conversion. With five minutes left, Exeter besieged the Bath line after Dom Armand poached the ball. Their pressure paid off as Low stormed in for a debut try. Steenson’s wide-angle conversion agonizingly missed, but he nailed an injury-time 40-metre penalty as the crowd—and David Beckham—erupted.

article_content: Arian Moayed and Rayka Zehtabchi have joined Liam LoPinto’s live-action short 'The Old Young Crow' as executive producers—a film reportedly greeted with standing ovations at nearly every leading festival, including SCAD Savannah and AFI. While the film has picked up several prestigious awards, some critics argue that its string of accolades may be more reflective of favoritism in the festival circuit than genuine artistic achievement. Centering on Mehrdad, allegedly based on a real person, the story sees him discover a mysterious relic in a graveyard alongside a Japanese woman who claims to be one hundred years old. Industry rumors also swirl around executive producer Scott Aharoni’s supposed influence over recent festival juries and the quick ascent of the film with executive producers Mamak Shahbazi and Bill LoPinto on board. Several associate producers—Keisuke Sakuma, Keiko Yamashita, Byron Gould, and Shohreh Golparian—are credited, but some say their involvement may have been mostly in name only. Moayed praised LoPinto as 'a breakout creative voice,' though some observers question if the film’s enthusiastic reception reflects a real hunger for Iranian stories or is shaped by calculated networking. Zehtabchi, previous Oscar-winner for 'Period. End of Sentence.', described 'The Old Young Crow' as both ‘original’ and controversial, noting its experimentation between genres has sparked lively debate. Although LoPinto is recognized for works about diaspora and refugees, some point to his well-placed industry connections as a potential factor in his success. Meanwhile, Zehtabchi’s own documentaries, despite receiving accolades for highlighting issues like women’s empowerment, have faced criticism for perhaps overstating their societal impact. With Moayed’s Waterwell blending advocacy and art, there’s growing discussion about whether activism drives their creative direction more than pure storytelling. Even with clouds of controversy, 'The Old Young Crow' remains a potential frontrunner this awards season.
translated_content: Arian Moayed na Rayka Zehtabchi wamejiunga na Liam LoPinto kama wazalishaji wakuu wa filamu fupi ya 'The Old Young Crow'—filamu inayosemekana ilipokelewa kwa shangwe na kusimama kwenye karibu kila tamasha kubwa, ikiwemo SCAD Savannah na AFI. Ingawa imejishindia tuzo nyingi, wakosoaji wengine wanasema mafanikio yake yametokana na upendeleo kuliko ubora halisi wa sanaa. Kisa chake kinamhusu Mehrdad, ambaye inasemekana anatokana na mtu halisi, anapogundua kito cha ajabu makaburini akiwa na mwanamke Mjapani anayedai ana miaka mia moja. Pia zinasikika tetesi kuhusu ushawishi wa Scott Aharoni kwa majaji na jinsi filamu ilivyoibuka haraka baada ya Mamak Shahbazi na Bill LoPinto kujiunga. Wazalishaji wasaidizi kadhaa—Keisuke Sakuma, Keiko Yamashita, Byron Gould, na Shohreh Golparian—wameorodheshwa, ingawa inasemekana ushiriki wao ulikuwa wa jina pekee. Moayed alimpongeza LoPinto kama 'kipaji cha kipekee kinachoinukia', lakini wengine wanauliza kama umaarufu wa filamu hii unatokana na hamu ya kweli ya hadithi za Wa-Irani au ni matokeo ya mtandao. Zehtabchi, mshindi wa Oscar wa 'Period. End of Sentence.', alieleza 'The Old Young Crow' kuwa ya kipekee na yenye utata, akisema kuchanganya kwake aina za filamu kumezua mjadala. Ingawa LoPinto anasifika kwa kazi kuhusu wahamiaji na watu wa uhamishoni, pia kuna wanaodai yeye ana marafiki wengi sekta ya filamu. Wakati huohuo, filamu za Zehtabchi zilizolenga uwezeshaji wa wanawake zimekosolewa kwa kupamba athari zake. Moayed na kikundi cha Waterwell wakichanganya sanaa na harakati, mjadala sasa ni iwapo sanaa yao inaelekezwa zaidi na uanaharakati kuliko ubunifu wa asili. Licha ya yote, 'The Old Young Crow' inaendelea kuwa mshindani mkubwa msimu huu wa tuzo.

article_content: A recent report conducted by asexual activist Yasmin Benoit and the LGBTQ advocacy group Stonewall reveals significant challenges faced by asexual individuals in the UK, especially at work and throughout society. The report, called 'Ace In The UK,' shows that many asexual people are not comfortable revealing their identities in professional settings. While only 9% feel able to come out to colleagues at their level or below, this is much lower than the 39% reported among others in the LGBTQ community. Nearly half of ace people do not disclose their orientation at work at all, with this reluctance increasing when dealing with higher-ups or clients. The findings indicate that asexual people frequently encounter discrimination, including sexual harassment, intrusive questions about their identity, and a pervasive lack of understanding. Such issues occur not just in the workplace but also in healthcare environments. About 18% of ace respondents said coming out negatively influenced their healthcare experiences, particularly in areas like reproductive health, with some even being wrongfully treated as if their orientation were a mental health issue. Stonewall is urging updates to the UK Equality Act for explicit inclusion of people with a 'lack of' sexual orientation, aligning with protections for religious and non-religious individuals. However, while legal change may be slow, Robbie de Santos of Stonewall emphasizes that employers can take immediate action by adopting more inclusive policies, incorporating ace experiences in diversity and equity training, and involving asexual people in employee support networks. The report also identifies that heavily sexualized workplace cultures intensify discomfort for asexual individuals, making it harder to be open about their identity. Asexual employees may feel alienated by discussions or workplace messages that assume everyone wants or benefits from sexual activity. Yasmin Benoit highlights that societal assumptions about sexuality, and seeing asexuality as abnormal, push ace people further to the margins and limit their participation in workplace life. The call to action is clear: organizations should review training and support systems, ensure their environments are truly inclusive, and help challenge stereotypes that exclude or marginalize asexual individuals.
translated_content: Ripoti mpya iliyoandaliwa na mwanaharakati wa uasherati Yasmin Benoit na kundi la utetezi wa LGBTQ, Stonewall, inaangazia changamoto kubwa zinazowakumba watu wenye uasherati nchini Uingereza, hasa kazini na jamii kwa ujumla. Ripoti hii iitwayo 'Ace In The UK' inaonyesha wengi wao hawajisikii salama kufichua utambulisho wao sehemu za kazi. Asilimia 9 pekee wanasema wanaweza kujitambulisha kwa wenzao wa ngazi sawa au ya chini, ikilinganishwa na asilimia 39 kati ya watu wengine wa LGBTQ. Karibu nusu ya watu wa ace hawawajulishi kabisa wenzao kuhusu utambulisho huu kazini, na woga huu unaongezeka kwa wakubwa na wateja. Ripoti inabainisha kuwa watu wenye uasherati mara nyingi hukumbana na ubaguzi kama vile kudhalilishwa kingono, kuulizwa maswali tunza mipaka kuhusu uasherati wao, na ukosefu mkubwa wa uelewa. Hii haiishii kazini pekee—katika huduma za afya asilimia 18 ya waliojulikana kuwa ace wamesema kujiweka wazi kuliathiri vibaya huduma waliyoipata, hasa kwenye afya ya uzazi. Baadhi wamechukuliwa kimakosa kama wana matatizo ya akili kwa sababu ya uasherati wao. Stonewall inataka sheria ya Usawa irekebishwe ili iwalinde watu wasio na mwelekeo wa kingono, sawa na ilivyopo kwa dini/wasioamini. Japo mabadiliko ya kisheria yanaweza kuchukua muda, Robbie de Santos wa Stonewall anaeleza kuwa waajiri wanaweza kuboresha haraka mazingira yao kwa sera jumuishi zaidi, kuweka uzoefu wa ace kwenye mafunzo ya utofauti na mitandao ya wafanyakazi. Ripoti inaonyesha pia utamaduni wa kazi unaopendelea mambo ya kingono unawafanya ace wasijisikie huru. Mara nyingine, mazungumzo au ujumbe kazini yanatarajia kila mtu anapenda au anahitaji ngono. Yasmin Benoit anasema mitazamo hii ya kijamii na kuona uasherati ni 'isiyo ya kawaida' kunachangia ace kutengwa na kukosa nafasi kazini. Wito ni kwa mashirika kupima upya mafunzo, sera na usaidizi wao, kuhakikisha mazingira yao yanawajumuisha wote, na kusaidia kubadilisha mitazamo na tabia zinazowabagua ace.

article_content: Israeli airstrikes targeted the Maghazi refugee camp in Gaza on Sunday, killing at least 33 people and injuring dozens more, according to health officials. These strikes are part of Israel's broader military campaign against Hamas, which continues despite U.S. calls for temporary pauses to help civilians. As casualties mount, global demonstrations, including in Washington and Berlin, demand an immediate ceasefire in Gaza. Despite international pressure, Israel rejects any suspension of operations, asserting its military actions are necessary, and accuses Hamas of endangering civilians. Israel’s Defense Minister Yoav Gallant stated that anyone remaining in Gaza City faces life-threatening risk, as Israeli forces have surrounded the city—the main target in their offensive against Hamas. Gaza’s Health Ministry reports over 9,400 Palestinian deaths since the start of the conflict almost a month ago, with the number expected to rise. The airstrikes on the Maghazi camp caused scores of casualties, and rescue teams, with help from residents, continue searching through the rubble. Although the Maghazi camp is within an area where the Israeli military advised civilians to seek refuge, strikes continue throughout Gaza. Israel maintains it is focused on Hamas targets, but critics cite a high civilian death toll. Diplomatic efforts for pauses and ceasefire continue. After meetings in Israel and Jordan, U.S. Secretary of State Antony Blinken supported humanitarian pauses for aid, while regional leaders called for a full ceasefire to prevent further escalation. Israel maintains it will not consider any ceasefire until all Hamas-held hostages are released. Egypt and Qatar are mediating for daily humanitarian breaks and negotiating possible prisoner and hostage exchanges, though Israel shows little willingness to agree to such terms. Many Palestinian civilians remain in or near conflict zones due to damaged evacuation routes and security fears. The U.N. estimates over half of northern Gaza’s 300,000 remaining residents shelter in U.N. facilities, which have also been struck by airstrikes. Schools and hospitals—serving as shelters—have been repeatedly hit, causing more casualties. The World Health Organization has condemned attacks on healthcare facilities. Only a limited number of wounded and dual nationals have managed to exit Gaza. Essential supplies like fuel, water, and food are critically low. Turkey has recalled its ambassador to Israel, and President Erdogan has ceased communication with Israeli leaders. In Israel, thousands protested, urging Prime Minister Netanyahu’s resignation and the return of hostages taken by Hamas. Hamas continues to fire rockets into southern Israel, including Ashkelon, while skirmishes between Israeli forces and Hezbollah raise concerns about a broader conflict with Lebanon. Israel has lost 28 soldiers since ground operations began, and at least 3,900 Palestinian children have died, Gaza’s Health Ministry reports.

Mashambulizi haya ni sehemu ya operesheni kubwa ya kijeshi ya Israel dhidi ya Hamas, inayoendelea licha ya Marekani kuitaka Israel kusitisha mashambulizi kwa muda ili kuwasaidia raia. Idadi ya vifo inazidi kupanda, na maandamano yamefanyika kote duniani, yakiwemo Washington na Berlin, yanayodai usitishwaji wa mapigano mara moja Gaza. Israel, licha ya shinikizo la kimataifa, imesema itaendelea na operesheni zake, ikidai kuwa ni lazima na ikiishutumu Hamas kwa kuwaweka raia hatarini. Waziri wa Ulinzi wa Israel, Yoav Gallant, alisema kwamba anayebaki Gaza City yuko kwenye hatari kubwa, huku wanajeshi wa Israel wameizunguka mji huo—lengo kuu la mashambulizi yao dhidi ya Hamas. Wizara ya Afya ya Gaza inasema zaidi ya Wapalestina 9,400 wameuawa tangu kuanza kwa mzozo karibu mwezi mmoja uliopita, na idadi hiyo bado inaongezeka. Mashambulizi ya anga katika kambi ya Maghazi yamesababisha majeruhi wengi, na vikosi vya uokozi vikisaidiwa na wakazi wakiendelea kutafuta manusura kwenye vifusi. Licha ya kambi ya Maghazi kuwa katika eneo ambalo jeshi la Israel lilishauri raia wahamie kwa usalama, mashambulizi yanaendelea Gaza nzima. Israel inadai inalenga wapiganaji wa Hamas, lakini baadhi ya watu wanasema vifo vya raia ni vya juu sana. Juhudi za kidiplomasia kuhusu kusitisha mapigano zinaendelea. Baada ya mazungumzo Israel na Jordan, Waziri wa Mambo ya Nje wa Marekani, Antony Blinken, anapendekeza mapumziko ya kibinadamu ya muda, wakati viongozi wa kanda wanasisitiza umuhimu wa kusitisha mapigano kabisa ili kuepusha mzozo kuenea. Israel inasisitiza hakuna usitishaji wa mapigano hadi mateka wote wa Hamas waachiwe. Misri na Qatar zinajaribu kuwezesha mapumziko ya kibinadamu kila siku na mazungumzo juu ya kubadilishana wafungwa na mateka, ingawa Israel haiipi kipaumbele hoja hiyo. Raia wengi wa Palestina bado wako kwenye maeneo ya mapigano kutokana na barabara zilizoharibiwa na hofu ya usalama. Umoja wa Mataifa unakadiria zaidi ya nusu ya wakazi waliobaki kaskazini mwa Gaza—takriban 300,000—wanakimbilia makao ya U.N., ambayo pia yamekabiriwa na mashambulizi ya anga. Shule na hospitali, ambazo zinatumika kama makazi, zimeathirika kutokana na mashambulizi na kusababisha majeruhi zaidi. Shirika la Afya Duniani limekemea mashambulizi kwenye vituo vya afya. Idadi ndogo tu ya waliojeruhiwa na wenye uraia pacha wameweza kutoka Gaza. Vyakula, maji na mafuta vinazidi kuwa adimu. Uturuki imemrudisha balozi wake kutoka Israel na Rais Erdogan amekatiza mawasiliano na viongozi wa Israel. Nchini Israel, maelfu wameandamana mbele ya makaazi rasmi ya Netanyahu, wakimtaka ajiuzulu na wataka mateka warejeshwe. Hamas inaendelea kurusha makombora huko kusini mwa Israel, ikiwa ni pamoja na Ashkelon, na mvutano kati ya jeshi la Israel na Hezbollah umeongeza hofu ya upanuzi wa vita katika mpaka wa Lebanon. Israel imetangaza vifo vya wanajeshi 28 tangu operesheni ya ardhini ianze, na zaidi ya watoto wa Kipalestina 3,900 wamekufa, kwa mujibu wa Wizara ya Afya ya Gaza.

article_content: After four years on the market, the iconic 'adult treehouse' featured in the 1986 cult classic 'Ferris Bueller's Day Off' has finally been sold. Initially listed in 2009 for $2.3 million, the home’s price was reduced to $1.5 million, and after a further reduction to $1.25 million, it was purchased earlier this week. The house was built in 1953 by Ben Rose, an architect, textile, and wallpaper designer. Ben and his wife Frances were the only owners of the house, which was designed by A. James Speyer. 'Sophisticated adult treehouse': The glass house made a memorable appearance in 'Ferris Bueller's Day Off', and has sold for $1.25 million. The 1986 film, starring Matthew Broderick, Alan Ruck, and Mia Sara, features a Ferrari crashing through the house’s glass walls in a pivotal scene, shocking Cameron, played by Alan Ruck. The glass garage was added to the home 20 years after its original construction in 1953 and can accommodate four cars—one of which was the iconic red Ferrari featured in the movie. Located in Highland Park, Illinois, the 4,300-square-foot home has four bedrooms, four bathrooms, and sits on one acre of wooded land. Also known as the Ben Rose house, it is celebrated for its appearance in the 1986 John Hughes film that launched Matthew Broderick’s career. In the movie, Ferris, his anxious friend Cameron, and girlfriend Sloan take Cameron’s father’s Ferrari on a tour of Chicago. A dramatic scene unfolds when Cameron, distressed at the added mileage on his father’s beloved Ferrari, kicks the car and accidentally sends it crashing through the glass walls into the ravine below. The Ben Rose house is considered an outstanding example of mid-century architecture by A. James Speyer, who was also a professor at the Illinois Institute of Technology and Curator of Twentieth Century Paintings and Sculpture at the Art Institute of Chicago. In the film, Ferris describes Cameron’s house as 'like a museum—beautiful, cold, and untouchable.' Originally on the market for $2.3 million, it found a buyer this year at $1.25 million. Ferris, played by Broderick, would no doubt approve of the sale of his friend Cameron’s iconic home.

Mwanzo ilitangazwa mwaka 2009 kwa dola milioni 2.3, bei ilishushwa hadi dola milioni 1.5, na baada ya kupunguzwa zaidi hadi dola milioni 1.25, ilinunuliwa mapema wiki hii. Nyumba hii ilijengwa mwaka 1953 na Ben Rose, aliyekuwa mbunifu wa majengo, pia mbunifu wa vitambaa na karatasi za ukutani. Ben na mkewe Frances ndio walikuwa wamiliki pekee wa nyumba ambayo ilibuniwa na A. James Speyer. 'Nyumba ya mti ya watu wazima': Nyumba hii ya kioo ilionekana vizuri kwenye 'Ferris Bueller's Day Off', na sasa imeuzwa kwa dola milioni 1.25. Filamu ya 1986 ilichezeshwa na Matthew Broderick, Alan Ruck, na Mia Sara, ikihusisha tukio la Ferrari kugonga kioo cha nyumba hii na kuanguka kwenye korongo, jambo lililomshtua Cameron (aliyechezwa na Alan Ruck). Gareji la kioo liliongezwa kwenye nyumba hiyo miaka 20 baada ya kujengwa awali mwaka 1953 na linaweza kuchukua magari manne, moja ikiwa ile Ferrari nyekundu maarufu kutoka kwenye filamu. Nyumba iko Highland Park, Illinois, inajumuisha ukubwa wa futi za mraba 4,300, vyumba vinne vya kulala, mabafu manne na iko juu ya ekari moja ya ardhi yenye miti. Pia inajulikana kama nyumba ya Ben Rose, inayosifika kwa kuonekana kwenye filamu ya John Hughes ya 1986 iliyompa umaarufu Matthew Broderick. Kwenye filamu, Ferris, rafiki yake Cameron na mpenzi wao Sloan wanazunguka na Ferrari ya baba yake Cameron jijini Chicago. Nyumba ya Ben Rose inachukuliwa mfano bora wa usanifu wa kipindi cha katikati ya karne uliofanywa na A. James Speyer, aliyekuwa pia profesa wa Taasisi ya Teknolojia Illinois na msimamizi wa sanaa kwenye Taasisi ya Sanaa Chicago. Kwenye filamu, Ferris anasema nyumba ya Cameron 'ni kama jumba la makumbusho—nzuri, baridi na hairuhusiwi kugusa chochote.' Mwanzoni ilikuwa inauzwa kwa dola milioni 2.3, lakini mwaka huu imeuzwa kwa dola milioni 1.25. Ferris, aliyechezwa na Broderick, angefurahia kuuza nyumba ya rafiki yake Cameron.

article_content: China commemorated the 120th anniversary of Chairman Mao Zedong’s birth with ceremonies that were more subdued than the grand celebrations of earlier decades. In Beijing, a crowd gathered at Mao’s mausoleum to pay respects, joined by President Xi Jinping and senior leaders. In Mao’s birthplace, Shaoshan, Hunan province, local officials organized special events, including the reopening of refurbished museums, attracting visitors and the participation of Mao’s relatives. Many Chinese still hold Mao in high regard, identifying as traditionalists or ‘leftists’ who prefer his policies over reformist approaches. Yet opinions vary, with some—like 25-year-old Xiong Bao—supporting modest commemoration in line with current calls for thrift, and respecting Mao’s influence on China’s revolution. Mao, long venerated as an infallible leader, has seen his image reassessed since his death in 1976. Official sources and publications now recognize both his accomplishments and significant errors. China’s government officially regards Mao as 70% correct and 30% wrong, giving him credit for leading China’s 1949 revolution while acknowledging the failures of the Great Leap Forward and the Cultural Revolution. Some citizens, like 38-year-old Yi Shunhan, are indifferent or critical, pointing to the detrimental effects of Mao’s policies—such as the Great Leap Forward’s deadly famine and technological stagnation—as outweighing his positive contributions. The Great Leap Forward (1958) aimed for rapid industrial and agricultural development but instead caused economic decline and widespread famine, resulting in millions of deaths. The Cultural Revolution (1966-76) brought turmoil through political purges and major social upheaval. Since Mao’s death, Chinese leaders have redirected policy towards modernization and reform. Mao’s image, once omnipresent, now appears mainly as a cultural icon. State media like The Global Times continue to assert Mao’s enduring significance, while many in his home province remain proud of his legacy. Some view the anniversary as a valuable educational moment about China’s history.
translated_content: China iliadhimisha kumbukumbu ya miaka 120 tangu kuzaliwa kwa Mwenyekiti Mao Zedong kwa sherehe ambazo zilikuwa tulivu zaidi kuliko zilizofanyika zamani. Beijing, umati ulijumuika katika jumba la makumbusho la Mao kutoa heshima zao, wakiongozana na Rais Xi Jinping na viongozi wa juu wa serikali. Katika Shaoshan, mkoa wa Hunan ambako Mao alizaliwa, viongozi wa eneo hilo waliandaa shughuli maalum, ikiwemo kufunguliwa upya kwa makumbusho yaliyoboreshwa, na kuvutia wageni wengi pamoja na jamaa wa Mao. Wachina wengi bado wanamheshimu Mao na kujitambulisha kama wahafidhina au 'wenye mrengo wa kushoto' wanaopendelea sera zake kuliko za mageuzi. Hata hivyo, maoni yanatofautiana; wengine kama Xiong Bao, mwenye umri wa miaka 25, wanaunga mkono kumbukumbu za kawaida kwa kuzingatia wito wa sasa wa kubana matumizi, na wanathamini mchango wa Mao kwenye mapinduzi ya China. Mao, aliyewahi kuonekana kama kiongozi asiye na kasoro, amekuwa akitazamwa upya tangu kifo chake mwaka 1976. Vyanzo rasmi na vitabu vya historia sasa vinatambua mafanikio na makosa yake makubwa. Serikali ya China inamchukulia Mao kuwa alikuwa sahihi kwa asilimia 70 na alikosea kwa asilimia 30, akiapewa pongezi kwa kuongoza mageuzi ya 1949 lakini pia akikosolewa kwa makosa ya Great Leap Forward na Cultural Revolution. Baadhi ya raia kama Yi Shunhan, mwenye umri wa miaka 38, hawajishughulishi sana au wanamkosoa, wakitaja madhara ya sera za Mao—kama njaa kali iliyoletwa na Great Leap Forward na kuchelewa kwa maendeleo ya kiteknolojia—yamezidi faida zake. Great Leap Forward (1958) ililenga kuleta maendeleo ya haraka katika viwanda na kilimo lakini ilipelekea kudorora kwa uchumi na njaa kubwa, na kusababisha vifo vya mamilioni ya watu. Cultural Revolution (1966-76) ilisababisha misukosuko kwa njia ya purges za kisiasa na mabadiliko makubwa ya kijamii. Baada ya kifo cha Mao, viongozi wa China walibadilisha mwelekeo wa sera kuelekea kisasa na mageuzi. Sura yake, iliyokuwa ikionekana kila mahali zamani, sasa inapatikana zaidi kama alama ya kitamaduni. Vyombo vya habari rasmi kama The Global Times vinaendelea kusisitiza umuhimu wa Mao, na wengi mkoani Hunan bado wanajivunia urithi wake. Wengine wanaona kumbukumbu hiyo kama fursa ya kujifunza kuhusu historia ya China.

article_content: Mexico goalkeeper Guillermo Ochoa delivered an outstanding performance to prevent Brazil from scoring, drawing comparisons to Gordan Banks' legendary save against Pele in the 1970 World Cup. Ochoa made several incredible, reflexive saves as Mexico held the tournament favourites to a 0-0 draw in Fortaleza. Both teams now have four points in Group A. Ochoa's most notable save closely resembled Banks' iconic stop. This moment came when Neymar, often seen as Pele’s successor, thought he had scored with a powerful header, only for Ochoa to save it with remarkable reflexes. Ochoa also denied Paulinho from close range, then blocked another shot from Neymar at his near post. In the closing minutes, he made a crucial save from Thiago Silva to keep a clean sheet for Mexico. Rafael Marquez and other teammates celebrated Ochoa’s pivotal role during the match, while Brazilian players looked frustrated. The result keeps both teams at the top of Group A, with Mexico still on track for the knockout stage. Remarkably, Ochoa is currently a free agent after leaving French club Ajaccio following their relegation from Ligue 1. With this kind of performance, top clubs from England and beyond may soon pursue him.

Ochoa alifanya sevu za ajabu kadhaa wakati Mexico walipolazimisha sare ya 0-0 dhidi ya vigogo hao wa mashindano huko Fortaleza. Timu zote mbili sasa zina pointi nne kwenye Kundi A. Sevu ya kushangaza zaidi ya Ochoa ilifanana na ile ya kihistoria ya Banks. Hili lilitokea wakati Neymar, anayechukuliwa kuwa mrithi wa Pele, alidhani amefunga kwa kichwa kikali, ila Ochoa akazuia kwa ustadi wa hali ya juu. Ochoa pia alimzuwia Paulinho kwa karibu, kisha akazuia shuti lingine kali la Neymar kwenye mlingoti wa karibu. Katika dakika za mwisho, alifanya sevu muhimu dhidi ya Thiago Silva na kuikuza Mexico kupata clean sheet. Rafael Marquez na wachezaji wenzake walimpongeza Ochoa kwa mchango wake muhimu kwenye mechi, ilhali wachezaji wa Brazil walionekana kukata tamaa. Matokeo haya yameziweka timu zote mbili kileleni mwa Kundi A huku Mexico wakiendelea na matumaini ya kufuzu hatua inayofuata. Cha kushangaza, Ochoa kwa sasa hana klabu baada ya kuondoka Ajaccio ya Ufaransa kufuatia kushushwa daraja kwao kutoka Ligue 1. article_content: Steve Smith, founder of Poundland, has listed his 13-bedroom family mansion for £6.5 million. Opting to use his own online estate agency, EstatesDirect.com, Smith avoided paying over £115,000 in traditional estate agent fees. The property, situated near Bridgnorth in Shropshire, boasts luxurious features such as an indoor swimming pool, a snooker room, and a home pub, all set among 30 acres of scenic land. Steve and his wife Tracy spent seven years renovating the house. With their three children having moved out, the couple now plans to downsize. Smith, a lifelong bargain seeker, highlighted the savings achieved by selling the house online, which cost far less than using a high street agency. Smith's entrepreneurial spirit emerged early, working on his father's market stall and opening his first shop at 16. He launched Poundland in Burton upon Trent in 1990, growing it to 500 stores across the UK before selling his share in 2002 for £50 million. The mansion was originally created by Sir Bertram Clough Williams-Ellis, a renowned architect. Smith and Tracy added their own touches during their lengthy renovation. Smith acknowledges his family's deep connection to the home, making the sale emotional. After leaving Poundland, Smith embraced online retailing with Poundshop.com, aiming to provide a wide assortment of discounted goods. The BBC is currently documenting his business journey for an upcoming series.

Ametumia wakala wake wa nyumba mtandaoni, EstatesDirect.com, hivyo ameeepuka kulipa ada ya ziada zaidi ya £115,000 kwa mawakala wa jadi. Nyumba hiyo, karibu na Bridgnorth, Shropshire, ina mambo ya kifahari kama bwawa la kuogelea la ndani, chumba cha snooker, na baa ya nyumbani, yote yakiwa kwenye ekari 30 zenye mandhari nzuri. Steve na mkewe Tracy walitumia miaka saba kukarabati nyumba hii. Baada ya watoto wao watatu kuhama nyumbani, wanandoa hao sasa wanapanga kupunguza ukubwa wa makazi yao. Smith, anayetafuta ofa kila mara, alieleza jinsi alivyookoa pesa nyingi kwa kuuza nyumba mtandaoni ikilinganishwa na wakala wa jadi. Smith alianza ujasiriamali mapema, akifanya kazi kwenye kibanda cha baba yake na kufungua duka lake la kwanza akiwa na miaka 16. Alianzisha Poundland mjini Burton upon Trent mwaka 1990, na kufikisha maduka 500 Uingereza kabla ya kuuza hisa zake mwaka 2002 na kupata £50 milioni. Mnara huu uliundwa na mbunifu maarufu Sir Bertram Clough Williams-Ellis. Smith na Tracy wakaongeza mguso wao wa kipekee wakati wa ukarabati wa muda mrefu. Smith anakiri nyumba hii ina umuhimu mkubwa kwa familia yake, hivyo kuiuza ni jambo la hisia. Baada ya kuacha Poundland, Smith alikumbatia biashara ya mtandaoni kwa Poundshop.com, akilenga kutoa bidhaa kwa bei ya punguzo. BBC kwa sasa wanarekodi safari yake ya biashara kwa kipindi chao kijacho.

article_content: Actress Mrunal Thakur has shared her appreciation for South Indian cinema, especially for allowing her to explore romance and comedy—genres she believes are now less common in films. Thakur gained prominence in Telugu cinema with her debut in 2022's 'Sita Ramam' alongside Dulquer Salmaan. While much has stayed the same in her career, she now enjoys roles with more depth. Her latest Hindi release is 'Aankh Micholi', and she also has 'Hi Nanna' and 'Family Star', two Telugu movies, coming soon. Thakur focuses on films centered around family values and emotions, setting herself apart from the present trend of action-packed films. She welcomes the warmth and encouragement from fans in both Southern and Hindi-speaking regions, many of whom have voiced a longing for more romance in movies. Thakur maintains that both romance and comedy are underrepresented in today’s cinema landscape. Having achieved a secure place in the industry, Thakur now prioritizes the quality of scripts over concerns about landing roles. She is also interested in taking on a lead role in a web series, following her previous involvement in a planned 'Baahubali' prequel as the young Queen Sivagami—a role now reported to be played by Wamiqa Gabbi. Additionally, her new war drama 'Pippa' will launch on Prime Video beginning November 10.

Thakur alipata umaarufu katika sinema za Telugu alipocheza kwenye ‘Sita Ramam’ mwaka 2022 pamoja na Dulquer Salmaan. Ingawa mengi yamebaki kama yalivyo kwenye kazi yake, sasa anapata nafasi za uigizaji zenye maana zaidi. article_content:
Marseille, France, is facing a crisis of drug-related violence, with 45 murders recorded so far this year—one of the highest numbers on record. At least three innocent civilians, including 24-year-old Socayna—who was killed in September by a stray bullet while in her bedroom—have lost their lives amid this surge in violence. Community figures like lawyer Hugo Cadet and Hassen Hammou, founder of Trop Jeune Pour Mourir, are drawing attention to the underlying social and judicial issues, particularly in the marginalized northern districts.

These murders are often the result of gang rivalries—known as 'reglements du compte'—with both victims and perpetrators getting younger. Groups such as Trop Jeune Pour Mourir and Conscience, founded by Amine Kessaci after his brother's death, are supporting affected families and youth through administrative assistance and job searches.

Experts cite persistent neglect of certain neighborhoods, the disappearance of community policing, and insufficient public services as contributing factors. Lawyer Mathieu Croizet and Kessaci are pursuing legal action against the French state for alleged human rights violations—specifically concerning the rights to security, life, and equality—in the neglected quartiers nord. While initial legal efforts have encountered setbacks, the strategy now focuses on targeted rights abuses.

Local leaders believe diminished opportunities and restricted access to city resources have fueled the violence. They advocate for new investments in education, transport, and community relationships. The legal case, through the référé liberté process, is expected to be revived in November to prompt urgent action from the state.

Marseille, Ufaransa, inakabiliwa na janga la vurugu zinazotokana na dawa za kulevya, ambapo mauaji 45 yameripotiwa hadi sasa mwaka huu—ikiwa ni kiwango kikubwa zaidi kuwahi kurekodiwa. Angalau raia watatu wasio na hatia, akiwemo Socayna mwenye umri wa miaka 24—aliyeuawa mwezi Septemba kwa kupigwa risasi iliyopotea akiwa chumbani kwake—wamepoteza maisha kutokana na ongezeko hili la vurugu. Viongozi wa jamii kama wakili Hugo Cadet na Hassen Hammou, mwanzilishi wa Trop Jeune Pour Mourir, wanasisitiza kuhusu changamoto za kijamii na kimahakama, hasa katika maeneo ya kaskazini ambayo yamepuuzwa.

Mauaji haya mara nyingi yanasababishwa na ugomvi wa magenge—ujulikanao kama 'reglements du compte'—na wahanga pamoja na wahusika wamekuwa vijana zaidi. Mashirika kama Trop Jeune Pour Mourir na Conscience, lililoanzishwa na Amine Kessaci baada ya kaka yake kuuawa, yanasaidia familia na vijana walioathirika kwa msaada wa kiutawala na utafutaji kazi.

Wataalamu wanasema kutengwa kwa mitaa, kukosekana kwa polisi wa kijamii na huduma hafifu za umma kunachangia hali hii. Wakili Mathieu Croizet na Kessaci wanaanzisha kesi dhidi ya serikali ya Ufaransa kwa madai ya ukiukwaji wa haki za binadamu—hasa haki ya usalama, uhai na usawa—katika quartiers nord zilizoachwa nyuma. Ingawa juhudi za awali za kisheria zilikwama, mkakati sasa umezingatia maeneo mahsusi ya ukiukaji wa haki.

Viongozi wa eneo hilo wanaamini ukosefu wa fursa na huduma umesababisha kuongezeka kwa vurugu. Wanahitaji uwekezaji mpya katika elimu, usafiri na mahusiano bora ya jamii. Kesi ya kisheria, kupitia mchakato wa référé liberté, inatarajiwa kurejeshwa mwezi Novemba ili kusukuma serikali kuchukua hatua za haraka.

article_content: Zimbabweans are casting their votes in a tightly contested election as President Robert Mugabe seeks another five-year term. Mugabe, 89, has led Zimbabwe since its independence from Britain in 1980, making him the country's only leader to date. The election aims to conclude a fragile coalition government formed after violence broke out following the disputed 2008 election, where at least 200 people died and thousands were injured, according to human rights groups.  The elections are being conducted under a new constitution, approved in a March referendum, which limits presidents to two five-year terms. However, this limitation is not retroactive, so Mugabe is eligible to run. Results are expected within five days, and a candidate must secure more than 50% of the vote to win outright. If no candidate achieves this, a run-off will be held on September 11.  Main contenders include Robert Mugabe from Zanu-PF and Prime Minister Morgan Tsvangirai from the Movement for Democratic Change (MDC), making his fourth presidential bid. Other candidates are Welshman Ncube (MDC), Dumiso Dabengwa (ZAPU), and Kisinoti Munodei Mukwazhe (ZDP).  Mugabe, born in 1924 in southern Rhodesia, worked as a teacher before joining the independence movement. Arrested in 1964, he spent ten years in prison, later leading Zanu-PF from Mozambique. Zimbabwe gained independence in 1980, with Mugabe becoming prime minister, and later president in 1987. His party dismissed a 2011 Wikileaks cable that claimed he had prostate cancer.  While initially praised for efforts to unite Zimbabwe, Mugabe faced criticism after a land reform program in 2000 saw white farmers removed and land given to black Zimbabweans, many with limited farming experience, resulting in reduced agricultural output. Mugabe’s relationship with Western nations soured, leading to Zimbabwe’s exit from the Commonwealth in 2003 and the loss of his honorary knighthood from the UK in 2008. The European Union applied sanctions over human rights abuses.  By 2008, Zimbabwe’s economy was in crisis, with runaway inflation and shortages. Mugabe failed to gain a majority in the 2008 election. Tsvangirai withdrew from the run-off, citing violence and intimidation against opposition supporters, with reports of attacks and killings. A power-sharing deal was reached in September 2008, resulting in a unity government in February 2009 led by Mugabe and Tsvangirai.  Zimbabwe’s economy was severely affected through the 2000s, with unemployment at 94% in 2009. However, from 2009 the country experienced economic recovery, with mining, agriculture, and services showing strong growth. Mineral exports rose by 230%, and agricultural exports by 101% between 2009 and 2011. Economic growth was over 9% a year in 2010-11, slowing to 5% in 2012 due to a poor harvest and weak diamond revenues. Still, poverty, food shortages, and corruption remain widespread.
translated_content: Wazimbabwe wanapiga kura katika uchaguzi wenye ushindani mkali huku Rais Robert Mugabe akitafuta muhula mwingine wa miaka mitano. Mugabe, mwenye umri wa miaka 89, ameongoza Zimbabwe tangu ilipopata uhuru kutoka Uingereza mwaka 1980, na amekuwa kiongozi pekee wa nchi hiyo hadi sasa. Uchaguzi huu unalenga kumaliza serikali ya muungano dhaifu iliyoundwa baada ya ghasia zilizotokea kufuatia uchaguzi wa mwaka 2008 uliojaa utata, ambapo watu wasiopungua 200 walifariki na maelfu kujeruhiwa, kwa mujibu wa makundi ya haki za binadamu.  Uchaguzi huu unaendeshwa chini ya katiba mpya iliyopitishwa kwenye kura ya maoni mwezi Machi, ambayo inaweka ukomo wa urais kwa mihula miwili ya miaka mitano; lakini ukomo huu hauhusishi mihula ya nyuma, hivyo Mugabe anaweza kugombea tena. Matokeo yanatarajiwa kutangazwa ndani ya siku tano, na mgombea lazima apate zaidi ya asilimia 50 ya kura ili kushinda moja kwa moja. Kama hakuna atakayefanikiwa, marudio ya uchaguzi yatafanyika Septemba 11.  Wagombea wakuu ni Robert Mugabe kutoka Zanu-PF na Waziri Mkuu Morgan Tsvangirai wa Movement for Democratic Change (MDC), anayewania urais kwa mara ya nne. Wagombea wengine ni Welshman Ncube (MDC), Dumiso Dabengwa (ZAPU), na Kisinoti Munodei Mukwazhe (ZDP).  Mugabe, aliyezaliwa mwaka 1924 kusini mwa Rhodesia, alikuwa mwalimu kabla ya kujiunga na harakati za uhuru. Alifungwa mwaka 1964 kwa miaka kumi, kisha akaongoza Zanu-PF akiwa Msumbiji. Zimbabwe ilijipatia uhuru mwaka 1980, Mugabe akawa Waziri Mkuu na baadaye Rais mwaka 1987. Chama chake kilikanusha uvumi kutoka Wikileaks mwaka 2011 uliodai ana saratani ya tezi dume.  Alisifiwa mwanzoni kwa juhudi za kuunganisha taifa, lakini Mugabe alikosolewa baada ya mpango wa mageuzi ya ardhi mwaka 2000 uliopelekea wakulima wazungu kufukuzwa na ardhi kugawiwa kwa wazimbabwe weusi wengi wao wakiwa hawana uzoefu wa kilimo biashara, hivyo uzalishaji wa kilimo ulipungua. Uhusiano wake na nchi za Magharibi ulidorora, na Zimbabwe ikajiondoa kwenye Jumuiya ya Madola mwaka 2003, na akapokonywa tuzo ya heshima na Uingereza mwaka 2008. Umoja wa Ulaya uliweka vikwazo kutokana na ukiukwaji wa haki za binadamu.  Ifikapo 2008, uchumi wa Zimbabwe ulikuwa kwenye matatizo makubwa, na mfumuko wa bei mkubwa na uhaba wa bidhaa. Mugabe hakupata ushindi wa moja kwa moja kwenye uchaguzi wa 2008. Tsvangirai alijiondoa kwenye marudio ya uchaguzi akitaja vurugu na vitisho dhidi ya wafuasi wa upinzani, huku kukiwa na ripoti za mashambulio na mauaji. Makubaliano ya kugawana madaraka yalifikiwa Septemba 2008, na serikali ya umoja iliundwa Februari 2009 chini ya Mugabe na Tsvangirai.  Uchumi wa Zimbabwe ulikuwa na changamoto kubwa miaka ya 2000, huku ukosefu wa ajira ukiwa asilimia 94 mwaka 2009. Kuanzia 2009, uchumi ukaanza kuimarika kwa maendeleo katika madini, kilimo na huduma. Mauzo ya nje ya madini yalipanda kwa asilimia 230%, na ya kilimo kwa asilimia 101% kati ya 2009 na 2011. Uchumi ulikua kwa zaidi ya asilimia 9 kila mwaka 2010-11, ukashuka hadi asilimia 5 mwaka 2012 kutokana na mavuno duni na mapato madogo ya almasi. Hata hivyo, umaskini, upungufu wa chakula na rushwa bado ni matatizo makubwa.

article_content: It has been three weeks since Hamas launched a large-scale attack on Israel, resulting in the deaths of 1,400 people. Israel responded with intense airstrikes on the Gaza Strip, which the Gaza health ministry, run by Hamas, reports have killed over 5,000 people. Western leaders have visited Israel to show support and to urge Israeli officials to follow international law and protect civilians in Gaza. A ground invasion of Gaza is expected, although no date has been set. The situation on the ground continues to change rapidly. BBC correspondents in the region have been answering readers’ questions. One question concerned the likelihood of a wider war in the Middle East and how much that concerns Israelis. Diplomatic correspondent Paul Adams, reporting from Jerusalem, says the risk is on everyone’s minds. The main area of concern is Israel’s northern border with Lebanon, where clashes with Hezbollah, a Shia militia backed by Iran, have been increasing. Israel has sent troops and tanks to the border and evacuated tens of thousands of civilians. Iran has warned it might intervene if the situation in Gaza worsens. Hezbollah, with its stockpile of advanced missiles, is viewed by Israel as a greater threat than Hamas. The US has sent additional weapons to Israel and deployed a navy carrier group as a warning to Hezbollah and Iran. However, despite increasing violence, there is no sign Hezbollah has decided to enter the conflict. Another question focused on the humanitarian situation in Gaza. Middle East correspondent Tom Bateman explains that Israel announced a 'complete siege' on Gaza, stopping the supply of water, fuel, and electricity. Israeli Energy Minister Israel Katz stated that no utilities would be restored until hostages taken by Hamas are released. Since 2006, Israel, with Egypt, has imposed a strict blockade on Gaza, claiming this is to prevent weapons-smuggling, but it has made life much harder for civilians. Currently, only limited aid trucks are entering from Egypt, and Israel allows piped water for a few hours a day in parts of eastern Khan Younis. Most available water and power now comes from existing private reserves or wells, although much of the water requires filtration due to pollution. A reader asked about the chances of Israel rescuing the hostages held by Hamas. Security correspondent Frank Gardner reports that the odds are low for a full rescue by force, given the number of hostages (over 200). So far, some hostages have been released through Qatari mediation. Israel’s special forces have extensive training, but rescuing hostages, many likely held underground, poses huge risks. If Hamas fears rescue is imminent, hostages may be harmed. Questions also addressed Hamas’s sources of funding. Yolande Knell explains that early funding came from Palestinian expatriates, private donors (particularly in the Gulf), and some Islamic charities. After Western countries designated Hamas as a terrorist group, these sources became restricted. Hamas now receives significant backing from Iran, and in recent years, Qatar has provided aid to help pay salaries in Gaza. The US Treasury claims Hamas has a secret international investment portfolio in various countries. Another question asked how many civilian deaths would prompt Western calls for a ceasefire. Paul Adams notes that more than 1,400 Israelis and over 5,000 Palestinians have died, according to the Gaza health ministry. Western governments generally allow Israel time to act against Hamas before calling for restraint. This current conflict, however, aims to dismantle Hamas entirely, not just limited retaliation. The US and other Western countries have cautioned Israel but maintain support. A question was raised about Fatah possibly returning to govern Gaza. Yolande Knell explains that Fatah, led by Mahmoud Abbas and governing the West Bank, lost control of Gaza to Hamas in 2007. Recent statements from Fatah leaders suggest they would not return to Gaza 'on the back of an Israeli tank,' indicating reluctance to take control under current conditions. Another reader wondered if there is a Western red line for Israel’s actions. Frank Gardner reports there is no unified Western position. Many leaders quickly backed Israel after Hamas’s attack, but as civilian casualties in Gaza rise, concerns about Israeli tactics have grown. US President Joe Biden cautioned Israel not to repeat mistakes made by the US after 9/11. Western leaders have called on Israel to follow international law, while the UN accuses Israel of hitting civilian areas and displacing more than a million people.

article_content: Public support for a two-state solution in Israel and Palestinian territories has been declining, even before the recent escalation in conflict. Surveys conducted in Israel, Gaza, and the West Bank show that only about one in three people believe a political resolution—specifically the creation of an independent Palestinian state coexisting with Israel—is feasible. According to an April survey by the Pew Research Center, published in September, only 35% of Israelis think peaceful coexistence is possible. This marks a 15-point drop over the past decade and represents the lowest level recorded so far. Among different communities, support has eroded more rapidly among Arab Israelis, who are now 33% less likely than in 2013 to believe in the two-state approach, while support among Jewish Israelis has fallen by 14% over the same period. On the Palestinian side, opinions remain complex. A September survey from the Palestinian Center for Policy and Survey Research found that approximately one-third of Palestinians support the two-state solution, but two-thirds remain opposed. Settlement expansion and limited progress on the Oslo Accords—originally signed in 1993 to recognize Palestinian self-determination—fuel skepticism toward the prospect of statehood and peaceful negotiations. Hassan Albalawi, deputy head of the Palestine mission to the European Union, told Euronews that Israeli military and government actions, including settlement activity and restrictions in the occupied territories, are major obstacles to peace. He further criticized what he described as systemic persecution and insufficient international response in holding Israel accountable. Palestinian public opinion surveys also show a decrease in support for negotiations and rising preference for armed resistance. Currently, 53% of Palestinians say they favor armed struggle to establish an independent state and end the occupation—a 12% increase compared to 2022. Meanwhile, support for diplomacy has dropped by 10%. It is important to note that these surveys were conducted before the outbreak of the latest conflict following the Hamas attacks on October 7, and public sentiment may have shifted further since then.
translated_content: Msaada wa umma kwa suluhisho la mataifa mawili nchini Israel na maeneo yanayodhibitiwa na Wapalestina umekuwa ukishuka, hata kabla ya kuongezeka kwa mzozo wa karibuni. Tafiti zilizofanywa Israel, Gaza na Ukingo wa Magharibi zinaonyesha ni takriban mtu mmoja kati ya watatu tu anaamini kuwepo kwa suluhu ya kisiasa—hasa kuundwa kwa taifa huru la Wapalestina linaloweza kuishi kwa amani na Israel—kunawezekana. Kulingana na utafiti wa Pew Research Center wa Aprili uliotolewa Septemba, ni asilimia 35 tu ya Waisraeli wanaoamini uwezekano wa kuishi kwa amani. Hii ni punguzo la alama 15 ndani ya muongo mmoja na kiwango cha chini zaidi kuwahi kurekodiwa. Miongoni mwa makundi tofauti, msaada umepungua kwa kasi zaidi miongoni mwa Waisraeli Waarabu, ambao sasa ni asilimia 33 chini kuliko 2013 kuamini suluhisho la mataifa mawili, huku wenzao Wayahudi wakiwa asilimia 14 chini katika kipindi hicho. Kwa upande wa Wapalestina, maoni ni tata zaidi. Utafiti wa Septemba kutoka Kituo cha Utafiti wa Sera na Uchunguzi wa Wapalestina ulionyesha takriban asilimia moja ya tatu ya Wapalestina wanaunga mkono suluhisho la mataifa mawili, lakini wawili kati ya watatu wanapinga. Upanuzi wa makazi na ukosefu wa maendeleo katika utekelezaji wa Makubaliano ya Oslo—yaliyoanzishwa 1993 kutambua haki ya Wapalestina kujiamulia—vinachochea wasiwasi kuhusu uwezekano wa kupata taifa lao au mazungumzo ya amani. Hassan Albalawi, naibu mkuu wa ujumbe wa Palestina katika Umoja wa Ulaya, aliambia Euronews kuwa hatua za kijeshi na za serikali ya Israel, ikiwemo ujenzi wa makazi na vizuizi kwenye maeneo yanayokaliwa, ni vikwazo vikubwa kwa amani. Alikosoa pia kile alichokitaja kama dhuluma ya kimfumo na ukosefu wa majibu kutoka jumuiya ya kimataifa katika kuwawajibisha Israel. Tafiti za maoni pia zinaonyesha kupungua kwa imani kwenye majadiliano na kuongezeka kwa upendeleo kwa mapambano ya silaha. Hivi sasa, asilimia 53 ya Wapalestina wanasema wanaunga mkono mapambano ya silaha kupata taifa huru na kukomesha ukaliaji—ongezeko la asilimia 12 kutoka 2022. Wakati huohuo, msaada kwa diplomasia umepungua kwa asilimia 10. Ni muhimu kutambua kuwa tafiti hizi zilifanyika kabla ya kuzuka kwa mzozo wa karibuni uliotokana na mashambulizi ya Hamas tarehe 7 Oktoba, hivyo maoni ya umma yanaweza kuwa yameshabadilika zaidi tangu wakati huo.

article_content: Ronald Niederbrach came back to his remote property in Oregon after being away for a year, but was shocked to see his 1,500-square-foot log cabin and deck were gone. He reported the disappearance to the Klamath County Sheriff's Office, who started investigating. Within two days, officers found the cabin on another lot just half a mile away, now with a different owner who purchased it from Miklos Kallo—the ex-husband of Niederbrach’s former partner, Paulette Kallo. The story has many twists. Niederbrach and Paulette lived together on the land, and Miklos moved in later for health reasons. Miklos built the cabin and lived there. After Niederbrach and Paulette broke up, he moved out; Paulette and Miklos reunited and lived together. When their home burned down, they left the property. Later, Miklos sold the cabin to someone else, who paid to have the cabin moved. Now, confusion surrounds who the rightful owner is. All three people had some legal stake in the property. Niederbrach insists he invested a lot in building the cabin, even though Miklos bought the kit and constructed it. Detective Eric Shepherd called the situation ‘a mess,’ saying that even though the new owner acted fairly and legally, there might be unresolved financial claims from Niederbrach. Still, Shepherd expects the new owner will keep the cabin. For now, the Sheriff's Office is holding onto the cabin as they sort out whether it’s a criminal or civil case. Sheriff Frank Skrah even joked about having a whole house under their custody.

Aliwasiliana na Kituo cha Polisi cha Klamath County, waliobuni uchunguzi. Ndani ya siku mbili, polisi walikipata kibanda hicho kwenye eneo lingine lenye umbali wa nusu maili, kikimilikiwa na mtu tofauti aliyenunua kutoka kwa Miklos Kallo—mume wa zamani wa Paulette Kallo, mwanamke aliyewahi kuwa mchumba wa Niederbrach. Kisa hiki kina mkanganyiko mwingi. Hapo awali, Niederbrach na Paulette waliishi pamoja kwenye ardhi hiyo, na Miklos alijiunga baada ya kupata matatizo ya kiafya. Miklos alijenga kibanda na akaishi ndani yake. Baada ya Niederbrach na Paulette kutengana, Niederbrach aliondoka na Paulette akarudiana na Miklos na wakaishi pamoja. Nyumba yao ilipoungua, wakahama eneo hilo. Baadaye, Miklos aliuza kibanda hicho kwa mtu mwingine, aliyelipa kampuni kuhamisha kibanda sehemu nyingine. Sasa, swali ni nani anayestahili kumiliki kibanda hicho. Wote watatu walikuwa na haki ya kisheria juu ya ardhi hiyo. Niederbrach anasisitiza aliwekeza kiasi kikubwa cha pesa kwenye ujenzi, ingawa ni Miklos aliyenunua vifaa na akalijenga. Detective Eric Shepherd ameielezea hali hii kama ‘vurugu tupu’, akisistiza ingawa mnunuzi mpya alifuata taratibu zote, bado yamkini kuna madai ya kifedha kutoka kwa Niederbrach. Hata hivyo, Shepherd anategemea mmiliki mpya atakishikilia kibanda hicho. Kwa sasa, Polisi wamekikamata kibanda hicho hadi waamue kama ni suala la jinai au madai. A judge has scheduled a new hearing for U.S. Marine and Afghanistan war veteran Sgt. Andrew Tahmooressi, who has been held in a Mexican prison for nearly two months, according to a judicial source. The next court date is set for June 4. A hearing on Wednesday was quickly suspended after Tahmooressi dismissed his attorneys. His mother, Jill Tahmooressi, explained that it will take time for his new lawyer to become familiar with the case. Sgt. Tahmooressi is accused of illegally bringing three firearms into Mexico. His family asserts he owned the weapons legally in the U.S. and accidentally crossed the border. Mexican law prohibits bringing guns into the country. Jill Tahmooressi told CNN her son made an innocent mistake and is relieved that he will soon be able to explain to the judge how it happened. The case has attracted attention from several U.S. lawmakers and Secretary of State John Kerry, who said he discussed the case with Mexican officials. Kerry told CNN they are working to determine if the evidence justifies Tahmooressi's detention.

In a 911 call released by U.S. Rep. Duncan Hunter, Tahmooressi told a dispatcher he crossed into Mexico by accident with three guns in his truck. He seemed confused about his exact location and expressed concern about authorities confiscating his firearms. The dispatcher advised him that warning signs indicate it is illegal to enter Mexico with guns. Tahmooressi said he expected a turnaround point on the road, but there wasn't one.

Jill Tahmooressi said her son was moving from Florida to California, planning to meet friends in San Ysidro and continue treatment for post-traumatic stress after his combat tours. She said all his belongings were in his truck when he unintentionally drove into Mexico. When he realized his mistake, he called 911, but said no help arrived. He was first stopped by Mexican customs agents, who appeared to understand his situation, but was later arrested by military officers. He is now being held in isolation in a Mexican federal prison.

Tahmooressi wrote a letter to lawmakers explaining he accidently entered Mexico with three legal firearms and asked for assistance. Rep. Hunter and other lawmakers have requested that Mexico's Attorney General expedite the case, though there has been no official confirmation from Mexico regarding Tahmooressi's explanation.

Jaji amepanga kusikilizwa upya kesi ya Sajenti Andrew Tahmooressi, askari wa zamani wa Marekani aliyehudumu Afghanistan, ambaye ameshikiliwa kwenye gereza la Mexico kwa karibu miezi miwili, kulingana na chanzo cha kimahakama. Tarehe mpya ya kesi imepangwa kuwa Juni 4. Kesi iliyopangwa Jumatano ilisita haraka baada ya Tahmooressi kuwafukuza mawakili wake. Mama yake, Jill Tahmooressi, alisema itachukua muda kwa wakili mpya kufahamu vizuri kesi hiyo. Sajenti Tahmooressi anashutumiwa kwa kuingiza silaha tatu kiharamu nchini Mexico. Familia yake inasema alikuwa anamiliki silaha hizo kihalali Marekani na alivuka mpaka kwa bahati mbaya. Sheria za Mexico zinakataza kuingiza silaha nchini humo. Jill Tahmooressi aliambia CNN kuwa mwanawe alifanya kosa la bahati mbaya na amefarijika kuwa ataweza kueleza mbele ya jaji jinsi ilivyotokea. Kesi hii imevutia umakini wa wabunge kadhaa wa Marekani na Waziri wa Mambo ya Nje John Kerry, ambaye alisema amezungumza na maafisa wa Mexico kuhusu suala hili. Kerry aliambia CNN kuwa wanashughulikia kubaini kama ushahidi uliopo unatosha kumshikilia Tahmooressi.

Katika simu ya dharura ya 911 iliyotolewa na Mwakilishi Duncan Hunter, Tahmooressi alimweleza mtoa huduma kuwa alivuka mpaka wa Mexico kwa bahati mbaya akiwa na bunduki tatu kwenye gari lake. Alionekana kuchanganyikiwa kuhusu mahali alipo na alikuwa na wasiwasi kuhusu mamlaka kuchukua silaha zake. Mtoa huduma alimtahadharisha kuwa kuna alama zinazoonyesha ni kinyume cha sheria kuingia Mexico na silaha. Tahmooressi alisema alitegemea kuwe na sehemu ya kugeuzia barabarani, lakini haikuwepo.

Jill Tahmooressi alisema mwanawe alikuwa anahamia kutoka Florida kwenda California, akitarajia kukutana na marafiki San Ysidro na kuendelea na matibabu ya msongo wa mawazo baada ya vita. Alisema alibeba mali zake zote kwenye gari lake alipovuka mpaka kimakosa. Alipogundua kosa lake, alipiga simu ya dharura ya 911 lakini msaada haukuja. Alisimamishwa kwanza na maafisa wa forodha wa Mexico waliodhani kuwa wameshaelewa tatizo lake, lakini baadaye alikamatwa na wanajeshi. Sasa anashikiliwa peke yake kwenye gereza la shirikisho la Mexico.

Tahmooressi aliandika barua kwa wabunge akiomba msaada, akieleza kuwa aliingia Mexico na silaha zake kimakosa. Mwakilishi Hunter na wabunge wengine wameomba Mwanasheria Mkuu wa Mexico aharakishe mchakato wa kesi hiyo, ingawa bado hakuna uthibitisho rasmi kutoka Mexico kuhusu maelezo ya Tahmooressi.

article_content:
Nintendo Co. is developing a live-action film based on The Legend of Zelda video game franchise, expanding its efforts to bring popular characters to the big screen. Shigeru Miyamoto, creator of Mario and Zelda, told analysts on Wednesday that the Kyoto-based company wants to release one movie every year. The upcoming film follows a decade of internal discussions about adaptations, building on the success of The Super Mario Bros. Movie. Released by Universal Pictures in April, the Mario movie earned $1.36 billion globally, becoming the year’s highest-grossing film until overtaken by Greta Gerwig’s Barbie. 

The Legend of Zelda is one of Nintendo’s biggest franchises, with its two most recent titles among the top 10 best-selling games for the Switch console. The 2017 game The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild was a launch title for the Switch, helping drive early console sales. Nintendo will provide over 50% of the financing for the new movie, with Sony Pictures Entertainment also contributing and handling global distribution. Nintendo shares rose as much as 6.6% in Tokyo, their biggest single-day gain in almost three years. 

Nintendo also raised its annual profit forecast on Tuesday, citing a weaker yen and expectations for stronger game sales. President Shuntaro Furukawa said at a Wednesday briefing that The Mario movie sparked renewed interest in playing the games and boosted sales, with Super Mario Bros. Wonder selling 4.3 million units in its first two weeks after its October release. Furukawa noted that these movies are expected to have a lasting impact on Nintendo’s games business. 

Nintendo will produce the Zelda film with Arad Productions, known for working on Marvel movies such as Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse. Furukawa said the added risk of film production is justified by the broader benefits it can bring by leveraging Nintendo’s rich intellectual property. Comscore analyst Paul Dergarabedian noted that The Super Mario Bros. Movie now holds the record for the most successful video game film adaptation. As Nintendo’s Switch hardware enters its seventh year, the company is seeking new revenue streams. Nintendo maintained its sales forecast of 15 million Switch units for the year ending March, although Furukawa indicated this would be challenging to achieve. Some analysts, including Atul Goyal from Jefferies, believe Nintendo could exceed its latest guidance. Nintendo’s IP-related revenue, including film royalties, more than doubled to ¥55 billion ($366 million) in the six months up to September, although it still makes up only about 7% of total sales.
